name: Calvary Chapel: Beginnings and Splits
summary: How a small church in Costa Mesa, California, under Chuck Smith became the home of the Jesus Movement and a worldwide fellowship of churches, and how the Vineyard and later groups split from it.

start.label: Chuck Smith becomes pastor of Calvary Chapel in Costa Mesa, a congregation of about 25

end.label: Calvary Chapel Costa Mesa leads churches into the new Calvary Chapel Association, separate from the Global Network

key_dates.label: Hippie evangelist Lonnie Frisbee joins; young converts pour in
Maranatha! Music founded; Time features the 'Jesus Revolution'
John Wimber's churches leave to form the Vineyard

background.text: Chuck Smith, a pastor from the Foursquare denomination, took over a struggling independent church in Costa Mesa in 1965, as the counterculture grew in Southern California.

happened.text: With Lonnie Frisbee, Smith reached hippies and young people; the church held mass baptisms in the Pacific at Pirate's Cove, and thousands were converted in what became known as the Jesus Movement.
Calvary Chapel combined verse-by-verse Bible teaching, informal dress, and contemporary worship music, spread through Maranatha! Music (1971).
Pastors trained at Costa Mesa planted hundreds of churches in a loose fellowship rather than a denomination.
Smith dismissed Frisbee over his ministry style, and later disagreements over charismatic practice led John Wimber's group to leave in 1982.

participants.name: Chuck Smith
participants.role: Founding pastor of Calvary Chapel Costa Mesa

participants.name: Lonnie Frisbee
participants.role: Jesus Movement evangelist; later left and died in 1993

participants.name: Brian Brodersen
participants.role: Smith's son-in-law and successor at Costa Mesa

outcomes.text: Calvary Chapel grew to well over 1,000 affiliated churches and strongly influenced American evangelical worship and church style.

persecution_note: Calvary Chapel faced no persecution; its divisions came through disagreements among its leaders.
